doc.title: Jack DeJohnette — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: New York and the Lloyd quartet
title: Charles Lloyd Quartet signs with Atlantic and records Dreamweaver
summary: Manager George Avakian gets the quartet an Atlantic contract; rock and the British Invasion arrive.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: No. It'll come. Anyway, we started doing Charles with the quartet, we started playing Slug’s and we started playing The Left Bank Jazz Society. Charles had a manager named George Avakian who had done some work with Sonny and Miles. George worked at Columbia Records and so George got Charles a contract… …Well, Charles had been working with Chico Hamilton and he'd done "Forest Flower" with Gabor and so George got Charles a contract with Atlantic Records. So, subsequently we went in and did Dreamweaver, and of course at this point in time The Beatles had come around. The British Invasion. Rock had come on the scene, Hendrix. It was a real interesting, what, ‘68? I think around…
We're in 66' at this point if you're just forming Charles Lloyd...
